verdict.reasoning: Patient describes dizziness with room spinning and unsteady walking starting about two hours ago: 'my room is sort of spinning and I can't walk properly... Started probably about two hours ago maybe.'
'my ears are buzzing a bit' directly supports ear buzzing.
Patient reports feeling sick: 'No, but I am feeling very sick.' Doctor clarifies as 'Nausea.'
Dizziness with room spinning and unsteady gait for ~2 hours is described: 'my room is sort of spinning and I can't walk properly... Started probably about two hours ago maybe.'
Patient notes buzzing without pain or discharge: 'you have some ear buzzing... Any kind of ear pain or ear discharge? ... Patient: No, nothing.'
Patient has nausea but no vomiting: 'Have you been physically sick? Patient: No, but I am feeling very sick. Doctor: Nausea.'
Prior similar brief episode: 'I had it a similar sort of thing about a month ago... Probably only about five, ten minutes.'
No recent viral illness: 'Did you have any kind of viral illness in the recent past?... Patient: No.' and 'No cold, cough, nothing? Patient: No.'

Fever is addressed only as current temperature: 'Do you have a temperature at all? Patient: I don't think so.' There is no statement about *recent* fever, so specifying no recent fever adds information not in the transcript.
'Is there any medical conditions you'd like to tell me?... Patient: I've had premature ovarian failure.'
Patient links HRT to premature ovarian failure: 'I've had premature ovarian failure and I've taken hrt.'
No other medications: 'And any other medications at all? Patient: No.'

Doctor plans Semitol (a vestibular sedative) 1 tablet TID for 10 days: 'It's called semitol. Yep. It's one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about 10 days worth.' This is consistent with meclizine (Semitol) for symptomatic relief.
Paracetamol is used only as an analogy: 'Like, if you have a fever, we just give paracetamol.' It is not specifically recommended to this patient as part of the plan.
No allergies: 'Do you have any allergies at all? Patient: No.'
No vitals or exam findings are documented in the transcript; the doctor only states plans to examine BP and gait later.

Doctor explicitly assesses likely labyrinthitis: 'the most common... diagnosis we would... you're suffering from at the moment is something called labyrinthitis,' based on spinning sensation and ear buzzing and prior similar episode.
Premature ovarian failure and HRT are mentioned, but there is no assessment of it being 'stable' in the transcript.
Plan to start Semitol 1 tablet TID for about 10 days: 'we'll start you on certain medications... It's called semitol... one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about 10 days worth.'

In-person examination including ears, BP, gait: 'I would still like you to be seen by one of our doctors to take a look inside your ears... we'd like to do your blood pressure, just examine your, you know, you know, how you're walking, and everything.' ENT vs general medicine specialty is not specified but arranging in-person exam is clear.
Emergency care advice for new weakness: 'if you develop any weakness of your legs or arms... then, you know, you would need to take yourself to A and E.'
Emergency care advice for severe headache: 'if you develop any weakness... or, you know, a sudden headache... you would need to take yourself to A and E.'
Emergency care advice for violent vomiting: 'or you start being violently sick with it, then, you know, you would need to take yourself to A and E.'
Paracetamol is only mentioned as an example, not as an explicit recommendation in the plan for this patient: 'Like, if you have a fever, we just give paracetamol.'
Follow-up appointment instruction: 'When... you're with the doctors...' and 'Just make sure you call support to book that appointment. Okay?'
